decisions.reason: As a niche but capability-fitting crate that was still shown in 2019, it likely sits somewhat below a large firm's aspiration level yet can be retained under organisational slack while demand remains uncertain.
Its dedicated product page in both 2018 and 2019 suggests comparatively strong acceptance versus aspirations, so management would be inclined to continue it.
A stackable plastic crate is close to the firm's established product logic, and continued mention through 2019 points to acceptable enough performance to keep it on the line.
The product remained visible after launch and fits the firm's logistics-plastics base, so boundedly rational management would more likely retain it than redeploy its resources immediately.
The move from a dedicated page in 2018 to only a mention in 2019 is a plausible sign of performance below aspiration, making resource reallocation more attractive.

Like E, its reduced prominence after launch suggests results disappointed relative to aspirations, and the firm would likely shift those moulding and sales resources to stronger products or new projects.
